entities.summary:
Alpin de Châlons (active in Baye, 400-480 CE) was a prominent religious figure of the Classical era.









 Alpin de Châlons played a pivotal role in the religious landscape of the 5th century, as a leader of a Christian sect in the region of Gaul. His efforts to spread Christianity were hindered by the collapse of the Western Roman Empire, but he continued to advocate for the faith.










 Alpin de Châlons' legacy is evident in the continued presence of Christianity in the region, and his influence can be seen in the development of the Catholic Church in Gaul. Despite the challenges of his time, he remained committed to his faith, leaving behind a lasting impact on the religious landscape of the region.











 A striking testament to his dedication is the preservation of a 5th-century manuscript, now housed in the Archives Nationales in Paris, which is believed to have been written by Alpin de Châlons himself.
